previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by chronic marginal (gastrojejunal) ulcer and post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring continuous gastrostomy tube feeds was admitted for recurrent severe epigastric and deep G-tube–site pain that worsened after an outpatient G-tube exchange and difficulty obtaining liquid oxycodone. Initial evaluation showed stable vital signs, normal labs, and chest radiograph without free air. CT abdomen with contrast confirmed the G-tube balloon in the gastric fundus with inflammatory changes at the abdominal wall insertion site but no hematoma, abscess, or discrete collection. Pain improved with medical management including liquid oxycodone and acetaminophen while continuing lansoprazole and sucralfate and maintaining continuous tube feeds with glucose monitoring. During the stay she developed asymptomatic hypotension felt related to atenolol and relative hypovolemia; atenolol was stopped and fluids given with improvement. She was discharged home ambulatory with a two-week supply of oxycodone, instructions to avoid NSAIDs, continue tube feeds and ulcer therapy, and follow up with her PCP and surgical/pain teams.
problems: Chronic gastrojejunal ulcer without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
Personal history of Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient presented to the Emergency Department on ___. Upon arrival to ED she was evaluated by the Bariatric 
Surgery team. A trial of steroid injection through the G-tube 
was attempted, however she had minimal effect with this 
intervention. Thus, she was admitted to the Bariatric Surgery 
service for further management.

Neuro: The patient was alert and oriented throughout 
hospitalization; pain was initially managed with oral oxycodone, 
then transitioned to oral dilaudid with better effect. 

CV: The patient remained stable from a cardiovascular 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored.

Pulmonary: The patient remained stable from a pulmonary 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored. Good pulmonary 
toilet, early ambulation and incentive spirometry were 
encouraged throughout hospitalization. 

GI/GU/FEN: The patient was kept NPO with tube feeds. A trial of 
bolus tube feeds was attempted, however the patient became 
hypoglycemic after each bolus was completed, therefore she was 
transitioned back to continuous tube feeds. Patient's intake and 
output were closely monitored during this admission.

ID: The patient's fever curves were closely watched for signs of 
infection, of which there were none.

HEME: The patient's blood counts were closely watched for signs 
of bleeding, of which there were none.

Prophylaxis: The patient received subcutaneous heparin and ___ 
dyne boots were used during this stay. She was encouraged to get 
up and ambulate as early as possible.

At the time of discharge, the patient was doing well, afebrile 
and hemodynamically stable. The patient was tolerating a diet, 
ambulating, voiding without assistance, and pain was well 
controlled. The patient received discharge teaching and 
follow-up instructions with understanding verbalized and 
agreement with the discharge plan.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to ___ with 
increasing pain at your G-tube site. You were given oral 
Dilaudid with good effect. While you were here, we trialed bolus 
tube feedings, but unfortunately you could not tolerate them. 
Therefore, we will send you home on continuous tube feeds 
(NutriHep @ 50 cc/hour). Please continue to monitor your blood 
sugars when you return home.

Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner or return to the 
Emergency Department for any of the following:

*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.

*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.

*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.

*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.

*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.

*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.

*Your pain in not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.

*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.

*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.

Please resume all regular home medications, unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.

Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids.

Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery while taking pain 
medications.

Please follow up with your surgeon Dr. ___ at the 
appointment listed below.

Best wishes,
Your ___ surgical team
